intro: ERS–WVSU connects scholars across disciplines with economic reasoning, empirical research design, data analysis, and causal inference. Our seminars are designed to move promising work toward credible, policy-relevant evidence.
section_one_intro: Research in agriculture, education, health, science, business, and other fields often raises economic questions. ERS–WVSU offers a focused space to identify those questions and develop the empirical strategy needed to answer them.
pillar_one_text: Clarify incentives, behavior, constraints, trade-offs, and the economic mechanisms behind a research question.
pillar_two_text: Discuss data, econometric specifications, identification strategies, uncertainty, and causal interpretation.
pillar_three_text: Explore joint research designs, stronger papers, policy analysis, and interdisciplinary grant concepts.
regional_text: ERS–WVSU welcomes research from any discipline when economic reasoning, quantitative analysis, or causal inference can meaningfully strengthen the work. The goal is substantive collaboration—not a general-purpose lecture series.
closing_text: Bring an early idea, a working study, or an unresolved empirical challenge. You do not need a finished economics component: discovering it together may be the first contribution.
